title: Scope reduction — Pricing & packaging
transcript:
Head of Product: Alright, let's dive into the product roadmap for Q4. Sales Lead, any updates from the field?

Sales Lead: Yes, I've been hearing some buzz about competitors launching similar features to what we've got lined up for Feature X. It's causing some potential clients to hesitate.

Finance Analyst: I've run some numbers, and if we push back the ship date by 3 months to include Feature X, we're looking at a potential loss of 15 sales in Q4.

Customer Success: That could mean a significant hit to our customer retention rates, especially since our competitors are already in the market.

Head of Product: I agree. Let's consider another option: shipping with reduced scope, which would allow us to meet the Q4 deadline and maintain our sales targets. Finance Analyst, what are your thoughts on the additional technical debt we'd incur if we went with the full scope?

Finance Analyst: With the current plan, we'd be looking at an estimated $30,000 per quarter in maintenance costs due to accumulated technical debt.

Head of Product: And if we raise the base package price to cover the cost of Feature X, we could risk losing 5% of our existing customer base and decrease sales revenue by 10%. Sales Lead, what do you think about this?

Sales Lead: It's a tough call, but I believe we should stick with our original plan and ship with reduced scope. If we delay Feature X until Q1 2023, it would give us time to address the technical debt.

Customer Success: I agree with Sales Lead. Feature X, while popular, has a low adoption rate and prioritizing it could jeopardize the development of other more valuable features.

Finance Analyst: I understand the rationale, but I still have concerns about the potential loss of sales revenue if Feature X is not included at launch.

Head of Product: I understand your concerns, Finance Analyst, but I believe the benefits outweigh the risks. Shipping with reduced scope will allow us to meet our Q4 targets and address the technical debt that would otherwise delay future development.

Sales Lead: Agreed. The sales team will need to communicate the reduced scope to potential customers and ensure they understand the benefits of the existing features.

Customer Success: The product team will need to prioritize addressing the technical debt accrued during Feature X development.

Head of Product: Alright, it's decided. We'll ship with reduced scope and delay Feature X until Q1 2023. Sales Lead, can you get in touch with the sales team and inform them of the decision?

Sales Lead: On it, Head of Product.

(Off-topic exchange)

Customer Success: By the way, have you heard about the new coffee shop that opened up down the street? I'm dying to try it out.

Head of Product: Oh, really? I'll have to check it out sometime.

(Back to the discussion)

Head of Product: Alright, let's get back to the meeting. Once the sales team is briefed, we'll need to start planning for the technical debt clean-up. Finance Analyst, can you provide an estimate for that?

Finance Analyst: I'll get back to you on that, Head of Product. I'll also keep an eye on any changes in the sales numbers as a result of the decision.

Head of Product: Great. I'll sign off on this decision and we'll regroup next week to discuss further updates and adjustments to the roadmap. Meeting adjourned.

Title: Ship with Reduced Scope and Delay Feature X until Q1 2023

The decision was made to launch with a reduced scope, postponing the implementation of Feature X until Q1 2023. This move aims to maintain the product's Q4 2022 launch date and avoid potential technical debt and associated maintenance costs.

A price increase to cover the cost of Feature X was considered, but it was determined that this could risk losing 5% of the existing customer base, decrease sales revenue by 10%, and result in a net loss of $50,000 in Q4 2022.

While Feature X has a high popularity, its low adoption rate suggests prioritizing it could hinder the development of more valuable features. Postponing Feature X will also provide an opportunity to address the technical debt incurred during its development.

The sales team will communicate the reduced scope to potential customers, emphasizing the benefits of the existing features. The product team will prioritize addressing the technical debt accrued during Feature X development.
